clue.text: Stropping lad from Seville?

parts.note: surface reading: a sulky, bad-tempered young man, a 'strop' being British slang for a tantrum
setter's reading: someone who strops a razor, as the hero of Rossini's opera set in Seville does for a living

explanation.surface: A moody Spanish teenager throwing a strop.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to be 'stropping' is to sulk; but a strop is also the leather strap on which a razor is sharpened, and Rossini's Figaro is the famous one from Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro, title character of The Barber of Seville, is a hairdresser who sharpens his razor on a strop.

clue.text: Help outside? Very keen

indicators.note: one word goes on the outside, wrapping round the next piece of the clue

parts.note: to help is to aid
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone asking for outside help, and very eager for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue in two: AID goes round V to give AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid and keen are synonyms, both describing someone eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Complaints on takeaway meat

parts.note: beefs is slang for complaints
split as take plus away: the four letters of take, sent away into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about the meat in their takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takeaway' looks like one word for a carry-out meal, but it splits into the fodder take and the signal away.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefsteak is a thick slice of beef, an example of meat.

clue.text: Start again on old writer

parts.note: re means on, concerning
O is a common abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin again on the work of a writer from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen something, such as a case or a shop, is to start it up again after a pause.

clue.text: Caught a couple of fellows and a German female with drug

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them
eine is the feminine form of the German word for a

explanation.surface: A police report: two men and a German woman arrested in possession of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German female' is not a person but the word 'a' in German, in its feminine form.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is a stimulant found in coffee and tea, so it is a mild drug.

clue.text: Wire tube that some subscribe to

parts.note: a cable is a thick wire
the tube is slang for television, from the old cathode ray tube

explanation.surface: A wired service you sign up and pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, since a cable service runs down a wire to the set; the wordplay is the two words Wire and tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable television is a paid service delivered by wire, so viewers take out a subscription to it.

clue.text: When and how to apply for a staff vacancy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British postage-paid reply service, by which applications can be sent at no cost
second meaning: an unfilled job is a post that is free

explanation.surface: Careers advice on applying for an open job.
explanation.walkthrough: You apply when there is a free post, and you can apply by Freepost, the Royal Mail service where the recipient pays the postage.
explanation.definitionFit: Freepost is a mail service letting replies be sent at no cost to the sender, and a vacant job is an open position.

clue.text: Time to muse

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Time to sit and think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' reads as a verb, to ponder, but is the noun: one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of love and lyric poetry, one of the nine goddesses of the arts.

clue.text: Satisfying foods merit new cuisine with nuts

indicators.note: cuisine is cooking, and cooking mixes ingredients up into something new

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A food critic praising a nutty new style of cooking as filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuisine' sounds like part of the restaurant picture, but it is the signal to stir the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriments are nourishing substances, food that feeds the body.

clue.text: It's set to go off with a bang

definitions.text: It's set to go off with a bang

parts.note: surface reading: an alarm clock, set to ring at a given hour
setter's reading: an explosive device primed to detonate at a set time

explanation.surface: An alarm clock set to ring loudly in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A time bomb is an explosive device fitted with a timer so that it detonates at a preset moment.

clue.text: Demands cutback by courts

parts.note: split as cut plus back: to cut is to axe, read backwards
CT is the abbreviation for court, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: Budget cuts imposed by the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' reads as one word, a reduction in spending, but it splits into cut plus the reversal signal back.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment or obedience is to demand it, often with force or authority.

clue.text: Heard playing all round the place

definitions.text: Heard playing all round the place

parts.words: Heard playing all round the place
parts.note: surface reading: a tune or band heard performing everywhere in town
setter's reading: sound reproduced through two or more channels so it seems to surround the listener

explanation.surface: A song that's being played everywhere you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereophonic sound uses separate speakers to give the effect of audio coming from several directions.

clue.text: Prize for cats' meat or fish, perhaps

parts.note: a medal is awarded as a prize
lions are big cats

explanation.surface: Awarding a prize for the best cat food made of meat or fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' meat' reads as pet food, but the apostrophe is surface dressing and the definition starts at meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Medallions are small round slices of meat or fish, so named for their coin-like shape.

clue.text: He is on about being present

indicators.note: one piece sitting on another means it comes first, with the other placed after it

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is going on about being present.
explanation.definitionFit: To be here is to be present in this place, the opposite of absent.

clue.text: Vaguely senses church is held to have distinctive properties

indicators.note: a piece that is held is gripped inside the other letters
something vague has no clear shape, so the letters are taken loosely in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A faint feeling that the church is thought to have special qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is the intrinsic nature or character that distinguishes a thing, so essences are its defining qualities.

clue.text: Simple properties of spa water coming up on new site

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evian is a French spa town and its bottled mineral water

indicators.note: making something new means the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A property developer describing the simple features of spa water appearing on a new site.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiveties are instances or qualities of naivety, the innocent simplicity of someone unworldly.

clue.text: Order one eats in backstreet

indicators.note: placing something in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: split as back plus street: St, the abbreviation for street, read backwards
the Roman numeral for one
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone eats an order of food in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like one word for a side alley, but it splits into the reversal signal back and the word street.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the state of being neat, with everything in its proper order.

clue.text: Risk to let go boomerang

parts.note: to back a horse is to risk money on it
to fire an employee is to let them go

explanation.surface: Letting go of a boomerang is risky, since it may come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boomerang' is a verb here: a plan that boomerangs comes back to hurt its author.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme that backfires rebounds on the person who made it, just as a boomerang returns to its thrower.

clue.text: I love getting thank you letter

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to receive a thank-you letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Have a fixed idea of other bosses

indicators.note: an other version is a different form of the word, its letters set out another way

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Fixating on what other managers are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to be preoccupied with one thought, unable to let a fixed notion go.

clue.text: Should be kept secret, if I fit following form

indicators.note: following places the earlier words after the later one in the answer

parts.note: a form is a school class
taken as written
fit for a task is able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone worried that their figure is a secret to be hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Classifiable here means fit to be classified, that is, marked secret by an official.

clue.text: A most awful opening

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A truly dreadful start to a play or match.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a small pore or a surgically made hole in the body, a technical word for an aperture.

clue.text: Otherwise, it's an English college

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the London School of Economics, a college of the University of London

explanation.surface: If not anything else, it's a college in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Else and otherwise are synonyms meaning in other circumstances, as in 'hurry or else'.

clue.text: Doctor got out of bed in a bad mood

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
to rise is to get up in the morning

explanation.surface: A doctor who got out of bed on the wrong side.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a sullen, gloomy temper, a grumpy disposition.

clue.text: Lie in bed, poorly, as a result of eating such food?

definitions.text: Lie in bed, poorly, as a result of eating such food?
definitions.note: the whole clue describes food that is inedible, an adjective

indicators.note: something poorly is unwell and out of sorts, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Stuck in bed feeling sick after eating something dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the first four words; the whole clue then describes the food that put you there.
explanation.definitionFit: Food unfit to be eaten is inedible, and eating it would leave you ill in bed.

clue.text: When special forces do wrong, it can be a killer

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
the Special Air Service, Britain's special forces regiment
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: When elite troops misbehave, the result may be deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired or political murderer, a specific kind of killer.

clue.text: Heartless agent — staunch in practice

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
to staunch a flow of blood is to stem it

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted secret agent who is loyal in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like an adjective meaning loyal, but here it is the verb to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an established method or way of doing things, as is a practice.
